claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially a high-temperature single-phase BCC alloy.
Atomic-size differences and chemical affinities drive local solute partitioning during cooling.
Ordered B2 regions formed by differently sized atoms can cause lattice distortions in an Al-containing Co-Cr-Fe-Ni alloy.
Local lattice distortions and short-range chemical ordering reduce the energy barrier for a shear transformation.
B2-like ordered clusters serve as nucleation sites for transformation to FCC or another ordered phase.
The BCC-to-FCC transformation proceeds by a shear-driven mechanism.
Local solute inhomogeneities promote nucleation of FCC or related ordered regions.
Thermal aging enhances diffusion and allows the transformed regions to grow and alter the phase balance.
Slower cooling will produce a larger fraction of FCC or ordered precipitates.
Aging at approximately 750 degrees Celsius will increase the fraction or size of FCC or ordered precipitates.
Transformation products may exhibit characteristic orientation relationships and Widmanstatten plate morphology.
The proposed mechanism requires enough atomic mobility during cooling to establish local ordering.
An ultra-high quench rate suppresses diffusion and prevents the local ordering required by the mechanism.
The mechanism will not operate when the aging temperature is too low to activate the required diffusion.
The analogous Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy starts in BCC and partially transforms to FCC.
The Pitsch orientation relationship dominates FCC nucleation in Al0.7CoCrFeNi.
In Al0.7CoCrFeNi, FCC Widmanstatten plates are parallel to the parent BCC {110} planes.
A slowly cooled or equilibrated Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 sample remains largely single-phase BCC with minimal ordering and secondary-phase formation.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts that slower cooling permits ordering and increases FCC/ordered-phase formation, but defines the baseline as a slowly cooled sample that remains predominantly BCC with minimal ordering. Thus the nominal baseline is also one of the treatments predicted to promote the mediator and outcome.
